thread.title: Why Google’s Growth Potential Goes Beyond Search

author: Teresa Rivas
title: Why Google’s Growth Potential Goes Beyond Search
text:
Courtesy Google By Teresa Rivas Sept. 27, 2018 11:35 a.m. ET Google’s parent, Alphabet (ticker: GOOGL), may be synonymous with search, but investors are underestimating other parts of the business, argues Keybanc Capital Markets .
Where we were : Google has climbed 15% year to date, despite all the high-profile trouble for big tech.
Where we’re headed : Keybanc argues that smaller portions of Google’s business will keep driving profits and margins in the coming years.
Big tech hasn’t had the best year , and Alphabet is the second-worst performing of the FAANGs—a group that also includes Facebook (FB), the worst performer and down 3.8% year to date, Amazon.com (AMZN), Apple (AAPL), and Netflix (NFLX)—rising ‘only’ 15% since the start of 2018. Yet tech has still been a market leader, and the Street may be underappreciating some of Google’s less visible business segments, argues Keybanc Capital Markets’ Andy Hargreaves.
Newsletter Sign-up He reiterated an Overweight rating and $1,430 price target on the shares Thursday. Hargreaves broke out revenue estimates for Google’s cloud, Play, and hardware units, components of the “other” segment of the company’s revenues. That didn’t change his growth expectations, but it did leave him more positive on the stock. His research suggests the potential for better gross margins leading him to raise his estimates for these units.
Not surprisingly, he writes that cloud is the fastest-growing sub-segment for Google, but he sees Play as the largest contributor to gross profits. His estimates for revenue and gross margins for the three businesses “suggest a more optimistic total Company gross profit outlook than we previously estimated, while leaving room for margin upside” as the segments’ scale increases, he wrote.
Hargreaves raised his gross profit estimates for this year and next to $78.2 billion and $90.3 billion, from $77.4 billion and $89.2 billion, respectively. That nudges up his 2018 and 2019 earnings per share estimates to $39.65 and $45.13, from $38.71 and $43.87, respectively.
Hargreaves estimates that the Other Google businesses will account for a third of incremental revenue dollars in 2020. Those areas already have gone from contributing 10% of total incremental revenue in 2015 to 22% in this year. The further increase doesn’t seem like a stretch, especially given the strength in cloud and double-digit growth in Play and hardware.
Shares of Google were 1.6% higher to $1,213.46 in recent trading. The Technology Select Sector SPDR exchange-traded fund (XLK) was up 0.6% to $75.09.
